newsitem.title: VANUATU: RTRS-Vanuatu paramilitaries released from prison.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Vanuatu paramilitaries released from prison.

text.p: More than 100 Vanuatu paramilitaries arrested for abducting the nation's president in a pay dispute have been released from prison and reinstated after swearing an oath of allegiance to the government.

However, 23 members of the Vanuatu Mobile Force (VMF), including Major Noel Tamata who ordered the president's abduction last month, have been charged with kidnapping, a government official said on Thursday.
More than 140 of the 300-strong VMF force were arrested on Tuesday morning and taken to prison in the capital of the South Pacific nation, Port Vila.
Justice Minister Father Walter Lini said in a national radio broadcast on Tuesday that they would be charged with offences relating to the abduction of President Jean-Marie Leye.
But on Wednesday, 119 of those arrested swore an oath of allegiance to the government and were reinstated into the VMF, the government official told Reuters.
A further 23 VMF officers were later charged in the Vanuatu Supreme Court with kidnapping, he said.
The VMF, which is effectively Vanuatu's army, claim the South Pacific government has failed to pay them special duty allowances amounting to US$1.1 million since 1992.
Addressing the officers at Independence Park in Port Vila on Wednesday, Lini said some VMF officers may have been forced to take part in the abduction of the president.

"I would like to see that justice is done and those who wish to remain loyal to the government and the nation will return to normal duty, but those whom a commission of inquiry find to be initiating such unwanted actions against the government and the state will be prosecuted," Lini said.

On October 12, the VMF abducted president Leye from his home in Port Vila and forced him to fly to a nearby island for several hours. The VMF asked him to then represent them at an emergency cabinet meeting over the allowance dispute.
The cabinet resolved to pay the VMF the back allowance by the end of October, but no payment has yet been made.
The entire 300-strong VMF also went on strike in October over the pay dispute.
